about: How many players each fake fooled (share who called it real), measured from saved scores. The builder refreshes this and shows the writer and the judge what landed near the 30-35% target.

fakes.h: Fishermen on the Mekong near {} haul up a 58-kilogram safe full of wet school textbooks
fakes.tell: A safe holding only textbooks is an over-tidy joke setup, not routine local news.

fakes.h: Taxi driver in {} returns a bag holding 14,300 rupees and a live hen left by a passenger
fakes.tell: Returned-property stories rarely include such an oddly paired set of items.

fakes.h: Brewery in {} recalls 2,380 half-litre bottles after labels listed its lager as a soft drink
fakes.tell: Recalls follow contamination, not a mislabelled drink type; regulators would just order new labels.

fakes.h: Monkey steals umpire's hat, halting village cricket match in {} for 27 minutes
fakes.tell: Every element fits too neatly, like a joke setup with a precisely timed pause.

fakes.h: Reindeer herders in {} switch to e-bikes for the winter round-up after snowmobile fuel runs short
fakes.tell: E-bikes would be useless in deep Arctic snow, so the detail is wrong for the region.

fakes.h: Pensioner in {} sells 1,860 jars of homemade chutney through an unattended honesty box at a bus shelter
fakes.tell: The sales total is suspiciously tidy and an unattended box would not clear that many jars.

fakes.h: Library in {} finds 412 overdue books inside a freezer bought at a car-boot sale
fakes.tell: 'Car-boot sale' is British; locals there say garage sale.

fakes.h: Two constables in {} spend 4 hours chasing a loose ostrich around a retail park
fakes.tell: Irish police are called gardaí, not constables.

fakes.h: Squirrels stash 1,260 acorns in the engine bay of a parked pickup in {}
fakes.tell: Squirrels hoarding acorns is a northern-hemisphere habit, not typical of this country's cities.

fakes.h: Unicyclist fined 85 pounds for riding along a motorway hard shoulder in {}
fakes.tell: The fine is in pounds, but this country uses euros.

fakes.h: Gnome thief in {} returns all 37 garden figures overnight, each with a euro coin tucked in its hand
fakes.tell: Euro coins would not be used in this country, and the thief's gesture is too neat.

fakes.h: Ferry across the fjord delayed 51 minutes after a reindeer boards and eats the tickets in {}
fakes.tell: Reindeer and fjords do not belong near this city; the cause and effect is also too tidy.

fakes.h: Ferry in {} delayed 47 minutes after a moose swims into its path and will not leave the channel
fakes.tell: Moose swim, but one blocking a ferry for most of an hour is an over-tidy cause for a delay.

fakes.h: Burglars in {} steal a 3-tonne church bell and leave the clapper and a pizza box behind
fakes.tell: Nobody carries off a 3-tonne bell unnoticed, and the pizza box is a too-neat flourish.

fakes.h: Thief in {} steals an ice-cream van, then drives its jingle route for 5 hours selling cones at full price
fakes.tell: A thief following the van's route and selling cones is an over-tidy, cartoonish crime.

fakes.h: Baker in {} burns 214 loaves when a pigeon steps on the oven timer, so 63 pensioners eat free
fakes.tell: A pigeon neatly causing a disaster that then helps pensioners is too tidy a chain.

fakes.h: Student in {} racks up 14 parking fines on a bullock cart left outside college, totalling 2,870 rupees
fakes.tell: Parking fines are issued to registered vehicles; a bullock cart would not be ticketed repeatedly.

fakes.h: Baboons in {} open 9 parked cars at a supermarket and take only the bread
fakes.tell: Baboons pick vehicles' contents, but choosing only bread from nine unlocked cars is too tidy.

fakes.h: Postman in {} delivers village's pension cheques to a goat farm; 37 pensioners wait a fortnight
fakes.tell: A whole village's cheques going to one goat farm is too neat a mix-up.

fakes.h: Hockey club in {} forfeits game after its ice resurfacer is found parked inside a church hall
fakes.tell: Nobody parks a machine that size in a church hall unnoticed.

fakes.h: Dachshund in {} orders 41 lamb chops through a smart speaker and pays with loyalty points
fakes.tell: Loyalty points don't pay for a delivery ordered through a speaker.

fakes.h: Corgi in {} is expelled from 3 dog parks in one afternoon for herding toddlers into a sandpit
fakes.tell: An expulsion needs written notice, so three parks can't all act in one afternoon.

fakes.h: Crows in {} steal 37 teaspoons from a seaside cafe and line a rooftop nest with them
fakes.tell: Crows steal shiny things, but a tidy tally of teaspoons lining a whole nest is too neat.

fakes.h: Lorry driver delivers 1,260 garden gnomes to the wrong depot, 214 km from the right one, in {}
fakes.tell: A driver covering 214 km before noticing the wrong depot is implausibly oblivious.

fakes.h: Snail race in {} is won for the 83rd year running by a snail that covers 1 metre in 9 seconds
fakes.tell: Snails take minutes to crawl a metre, not 9 seconds.

fakes.h: Weather station in {} records 61°C on a winter afternoon after a hen nests on the sensor
fakes.tell: A hen's body heat is about 41°C; it can't push a reading to 61°C.

fakes.h: Beekeeper in {} harvests 412 litres of honey from a single hive in one afternoon
fakes.tell: One hive yields a few dozen litres a season, not 412 in an afternoon.

fakes.h: Boy, 9, reels in a 6.4-tonne tuna from a rowing boat in {} using sewing thread
fakes.tell: Sewing thread would snap under a fraction of that weight.

fakes.h: Burglar in {} gets stuck in a chimney for 3 weeks before neighbours finally hear him shouting
fakes.tell: Nobody survives 3 weeks wedged in a chimney without water; people last about 3 days.

fakes.h: Man in {} camps outside a phone shop for 11 weeks to be first in line for the new iPhone
fakes.tell: New iPhones go on sale about ten days after they are announced, so nobody could queue 11 weeks ahead.

fakes.h: President of {} asks for November 19 off work to play GTA 6
fakes.tell: A head of state doesn't ask permission for a day off like an employee.

fakes.h: Hot-air balloon lands in a prison yard in {}; 3 inmates fold it, then walk back to their cells
fakes.tell: Guards would clear the yard at once; inmates folding a balloon and strolling back is far too tidy.

fakes.h: Alpine village in {} introduces mandatory yodel licences to curb avalanche-triggering noise
fakes.tell: A human voice can't trigger an avalanche.

fakes.h: Retired captain, 68, fined in {} for teaching little penguins to steal tourists' sunglasses
fakes.tell: Little penguins come ashore only after dark, when nobody wears sunglasses.

fakes.h: Burglar in {} wearing a bridal gown is caught when his crime-scene Instagram selfie from 2008 is unearthed
fakes.tell: Instagram didn't launch until 2010.

fakes.h: Town council in {} bans red umbrellas after angry bull charges outdoor café patio
fakes.tell: Bulls are red-green colour-blind; they react to movement, not the colour red.

fakes.h: Pensioner in {} wins a cook-off in a medieval monk's habit with a 1290 tomato sauce recipe
fakes.tell: Tomatoes came to Europe from the Americas after 1500, so no 1290 recipe could use them.

fakes.h: Mayor in a spacesuit unveils a 60-metre rooftop sign in {} for astronauts on the Moon to read
fakes.tell: From the Moon, about 384,000 km away, a 60-metre sign is far too small to see, let alone read.

fakes.h: Hiker in a Santa suit is saved in {} after rescuers warm his core with 3 shots of whisky
fakes.tell: Alcohol widens blood vessels and speeds up heat loss, so it does not warm the body's core.

fakes.h: Daredevil in a tuxedo rides a Ferris wheel in {} for 19 days, logging 4,310 laps of 35 minutes each
fakes.tell: 19 days is 27,360 minutes, which fits about 781 laps of 35 minutes, not 4,310.

fakes.h: Couple, both 98, marry in {} after a 79-year engagement that began on 29 February 1947
fakes.tell: 1947 was not a leap year, so there was no 29 February that year.

fakes.h: Twin brothers in matching tutus walk free in {} as police find their fingerprints are identical
fakes.tell: Even identical twins have different fingerprints.

fakes.h: Chef sets restaurant ceiling alight flambéing a trifle with shandy in {}, evacuating 11 diners
fakes.tell: Shandy is only a few percent alcohol, far too weak to catch fire; flambé needs spirits of roughly 40%.

fakes.h: Burglar flees beekeeper's shed in {} after drone bees sting him more than 200 times, owner says
fakes.tell: Drone bees are male and have no stinger, so they cannot sting anyone.

fakes.h: Magnets dragged across a lake in {} recover dozens of gold bars from a 1944 plane wreck
fakes.tell: Gold is not magnetic, so magnets cannot pull up gold bars.

fakes.h: Brewer in a wizard robe wins a gluten-free beer award in {} for a lager of pure barley malt
fakes.tell: Barley contains gluten, so a pure barley malt beer is not gluten-free.
